It sounds like you might be referring to HOB in one of two common contexts:

### 1. HOB (House of Blues) – Music Venues/Events
If you mean a House of Blues venue or ticketing system isn’t working properly:
• Check their official website or app for service status updates.
• Verify your ticket via the official ticketing partner (e.g., Ticketmaster, AXS).
• Contact customer support with your order number if you’re experiencing issues with entry, refunds, or event changes.

### 2. HOB (Head of Business / Home Office Board / etc.) – Internal Systems
If this is an internal company system or software:
• Try clearing your browser cache/cookies.
• Check for scheduled maintenance on the provider’s status page.
• Reach out to your IT helpdesk with specific error messages.

### 3. HOB (Hardware/Device)
If you mean a physical device (e.g., a Hobart mixer, kitchen hob/stove):
• Ensure it’s properly plugged in and receiving power.
• Check for tripped circuit breakers or blown fuses.
• Consult the user manual for troubleshooting steps or contact manufacturer support.

Since your Zanussi ceramic hob’s back-right ring isn’t heating up, here are the most likely causes and troubleshooting steps:

### 🔍 1. Check for Basic Issues First
• Power supply: Ensure the hob is properly plugged in or connected to power. Try resetting by turning off the circuit breaker for a few minutes, then switching it back on.
• Control panel lock: Some models have a child-lock feature that disables certain zones. Look for a lock icon (🔒) and deactivate it if active.
• Cleanliness: Ensure the glass surface around the back-right ring is clean and dry. Spills or moisture can interfere with sensor-based controls.

### 🔧 2. Test the Ring Itself
• Try using the back-right ring on different power levels (e.g., boost, low, medium). If it doesn’t respond at any level, the issue is likely internal.
• Place a pot of water on the ring and leave it for 5–10 minutes to confirm no heat is being generated.

### ⚠️ 3. Possible Faults
If basic checks don’t resolve the issue, one of these components may be faulty:
• Heating element: The ceramic ring has an underlying heating coil or halogen lamp that may have burned out.
• Power module/relay: Each zone is controlled by a separate relay on the power board. A failed relay can disable one zone.
• Touch control panel: If your model uses touch controls, the sensor for that specific ring might be damaged or unresponsive.

### 🛠️ What You Can Do
1. Reset the hob: Turn off the power at the breaker for 5–10 minutes, then restore it. This can sometimes reset faulty control modules.
2. Inspect visually: If you’re comfortable and have disconnected power, you may remove the glass top (consult your manual) to check for visible damage to the heating element or wiring under that zone. Only attempt this if you are qualified.
3. Contact support: Since ceramic hobs involve high-voltage components, it’s safest to contact a certified technician.

### 📞 Next Steps
• Locate your model number (usually on a sticker inside the hob frame or in the manual).
• Visit Zanussi Support or call their customer service with the model number and issue description.
• If under warranty, arrange for authorized repair.

I tried the ring on different levels and the display shows the number but it doesn't glow or heat up at all. I'm not taking the glass off though. The manual cover just says ZHRN at the start, I can't find the full model number. How do I find it?

Since your hob’s display shows the power level but there’s no glow or heat on the back-right ring, this strongly suggests a faulty heating element (halogen lamp) or a failed relay/power module for that specific zone. The fact that the control responds confirms the touch panel and main board are likely okay — just not delivering power to that ring.

### 🔍 How to Find Your Full Zanussi Model Number
The model number is usually located in one of these places:
1. Under the glass top: Turn off the hob and let it cool completely. Look along the edges or corners under the rim where the glass meets the frame. There may be a sticker with the model number (e.g., ZHRN 840, ZHRN 650, etc.).
2. On the side or back of the hob: If it’s built-in, check the metal frame underneath or along the sides where the hob sits in the countertop cutout.
